The day before the Supreme Court’s disastrous decision to gut the Voting Rights Act of 1965, I signed the Maryland Voting Rights Act of 2026 into law, banning election systems that weaken the voting power of protected groups.

Even if Washington won't protect your vote, I will.

📍 Our second stop on the Delivering for Maryland tour: Prince George's County.

We've funded critical programs that help families avoid eviction, expanded support for those who need help with rent or housing support, connected more young people with mentorship and mental health services, secured record funding for local law enforcement so we can continue seeing drops in violent crime.

Last week, I banned ALL state employees from using insider information to make money on prediction markets. 

But it’s not a sudden revelation for me. On my very first day in office, I signed an Executive Order outlining the ethical standards and expectations that would apply to EVERY member of my administration.

Later on, I signed into law legislation that made Maryland one of the first states in the nation to require the governor to place their interests into a blind trust and we created a Pe

People all throughout Prince George’s County are going above and beyond to remind our young men and young women that they are loved and cherished. 

I’m proud of their work and I’m proud that we’re helping deliver the support that Prince George's County deserves.

We need national redistricting reform to protect the right to equal representation under the law, but Republicans in D.C. have REPEATEDLY rejected those efforts. I've said before, and my position remains unmoved: Until we have national redistricting reform, every state should stay part of the conversation

SCOTUS’s decision to kneecap the Voting Rights Act is a betrayal of the idea that in America, every vote counts.

Their decision will make it easier to discriminate, suppress, and silence voters who have already fought too long and too hard for the right to be heard.

238 years ago, Maryland became the 7th state to ratify the U.S. Constitution.

Democracy has never been a guarantee. Every generation has had to fight to protect and strengthen it – and that remains true today.

I’m proud that Marylanders understand this. Led by @OAGMaryland, we are fighting back against an unlawful attempt to interfere with states’ constitutional authority to administer elections – and later today, I’ll sign into law legislation to help ensure every voice is heard and every vot

There’s no passing the buck on this just because of federal inaction. Marylanders want action, and that’s what we’re delivering on.

Clayton Bump is a 100-year-old World War II Navy veteran who lives at Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, a now 4 Star facility.

For his service, he was awarded the American Theater Medal, the European Theater Medal, the Asiatic-Pacific Medal, the Victory Medal, and the Presidential Unit Citation. His own brother made the ultimate sacrifice in World War II.

When people complain about something being hard, Clayton tells them, "That might be hard, but try being 100."

Thank you to the Secret Service and law enforcement for their swift response at tonight’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner. I’m grateful everyone is reported to be safe and that the suspected shooter is in custody.

We will never stop fighting for those who put everything on the line for our freedom.

Effective immediately, Maryland state government employees are BANNED from using inside information from their jobs to make money on prediction markets.

Government officials should never be able to participate in prediction markets. It creates a conflict of interest for officials and encourages them to work for the markets and not their constituents.

My executive order makes sure no one in my administration will be able to line their own pockets through predictive markets.

The federal reclassification of medical marijuana is a step in the right direction.

Two years ago, I took historic action, pardoning over 175,000 cannabis possession convictions. It’s an action that helped Marylanders who were impacted by outdated laws.

I know from firsthand experience that reforms like these – when done in partnership – actually help improve people’s lives, and we in Maryland are going to keep delivering wins that help people.
